utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. First of all, I would like to ask Madam Registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-03-66-I, the Prosecutor versus Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Andrew Cayley. I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor with my colleague, Mr. Colin Black and our case manager Ms. Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you and for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Peter Murphy or behalf of Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Steve Powles and I appear on behalf of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, my name is Stephane Bourgon from Montreal Canada and I appear this afternoon on behalf of Mr. Agim Murtezi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bala, would you please stand up. I will ask you some questions. Can you hear the proceedings in the language you understand? I didn't get the interpretation. Would you please speak louder.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I have your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is the date upon which you believe you were born.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 10th of June, 1956.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Where did you live before you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the place where I was born.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you tell me the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the village of Koretice E Eperme and it doesn't have any street names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Musliu. Would you please stand up. Can you hear the proceedings in the language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I have your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And what is the date upon which you believe you were born.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 31st of October, 1970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Where do you live before you came here? I mean in which village?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Recak in Shtime municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Murtezi, can you hear the proceedings in the language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Agim Adim Murtezi, born on 20th of February, 1956 in the village (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you have any nicknames, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the pseudonym of Gimi, Gimi [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down, please. We are here this afternoon for the initial appearances of the accused, in accordance with the Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, upon their transfer to the Tribunal. By the order of the president of this Tribunal, this case was assigned to the Trial Chamber I of which I am the presiding judge. I will ask some questions to the Defence counsel and those questions are addressed to all of you. Mr. Murphy, has your client received a copy of the indictment in the language which he understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes, he has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have a chance to go through with it with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I had a chance to discuss it with him this morning, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Does your client fully understand the nature of the procedure as well as his rights?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I believe he does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And does your client understand the counts of the indictment and he is aware of the nature of the allegations made against him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Powles. I think the same question, I address also to you. Can you answer them or do you need me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: If you could repeat them, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Has your client received a copy of the indictment in the language which he understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to discuss it with your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, briefly this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Does your client fully understand the nature of procedure as well as his rights?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he does, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And does your client understand the contents of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is he aware of the allegation made against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: He does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down. Mr. Bourgon, has your client received a copy of the indictment in the language which he understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. He has received a copy of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone. Did you have a chance to go through it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was -- it has been a bit difficult to meet with the accused today since I was assigned only later this morning. I did have a chance, however, to discuss with Mr. Murtezi for five minutes at the detention unit and just before the beginning of these proceedings for a period of 20 minutes; nevertheless, Your Honour, I can now -- I am now in a position to say that Mr. Murtezi understands the nature of the charges which are laid out against him in the indictment. He also understands the nature of the proceedings and as well of his rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In this case, to my understanding, the counsel do not have much time to discuss with his clients about their rights and the indictment. I will ask Madam Registrar to read Article 20 and 21 of the statute as well as the whole indictment in this courtroom. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 20, Commencement and Conduct of Trial Proceedings. 1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. 2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal. 3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. 4. The hearing shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Article 21: Rights of the accused. 1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. 2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the Statute. 3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present Statute. 4. In the determination of any charge against the accused, pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees, in full equality: (a) to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) to be tried without undue delay; (d) to be tried in his presence, and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing; to be informed, if he does not have legal assistance, of this right; and to have legal assistance assigned to him, in any case where the interests of justice so require, and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; (e) to examine, or have examined, the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f) to have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal; (g) not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The indictment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-03-66-I, indictment, the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (hereinafter the Statute of the Tribunal), charges: Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, Agim Murtezi with crimes against humanity and violations of the laws or customs of war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Haradin Bala, aka Shala, was born on 10 June 1957 in Gornja Koretica/Korotice E Eperme in the municipality of Glogovac/Gllogoc in Kosovo. At all times relevant to this indictment, Haradin Bala was a member of the KLA and a commander/guard at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. Isak Musliu, also known as Qerqiz, was born on 31 October 1970 in Racak/Recak in the municipality of Stimlje/Shtime in Kosovo. At all times relevant to this indictment, Isak Musliu was a member of the KLA and a commander/guard at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. Agim Murtezi, also known as Murrizi, was born 20 February 1956 in Cuculjaga/Qylage in the municipality of Lipljan/Lipjan in Kosovo. At all times relevant to this indictment, Agim Murtezi was a member of the KLA and a guard at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. Statement of facts: No later than early 1998 after years of increasing tension and violence, armed conflict commenced between Serb forces and the KLA in Kosovo. This development was consistent with the KLA's generally militant approach of active, armed resistance to Serb rule in Kosovo. Together with Serb civilians, Albanian civilians who were perceived by the KLA either as refusing to cooperate with or resisting the KLA by nonmilitary means were targeted for intimidation, imprisonment, violence and murder. Individual Criminal Responsibility: Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi are responsible for the crimes charged against them in this document pursuant to article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, as further specified below, for planning, instigating, ordering, committing or otherwise aiding and abetting the planning, preparation or execution of acts or omissions set forth in this indictment. General allegations: At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of armed conflict existed in Kosovo. All acts and omissions charged as Crimes against Humanity were part of a widespread and systematic attack directed against the Serb civilian population and members of the Albanian civilian population perceived as refusing to cooperate with or resisting the KLA by non-military means. At all times relevant to this indictment, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi were required to abide by the laws or customs of war, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and Additional Protocol II. Charges: Counts 1 to 2, Imprisonment, Cruel Treatment. From in or about May 1998 through to on or about 25 July 1998, in the municipalities of Stimlje/Shtime, Glogovac/Gllogoc, and Lipljan/Lipjan in Kosovo, Fatmir Limaj, individually and in concert with KLA forces under his command and control, planned, instigated, ordered, committed or other otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of the crimes of Imprisonment and Cruel Treatment of Serb and Albanian civilians. Fatmir Limaj also knew or had reason to know that the crimes of Imprisonment and Cruel Treatment were about to be committed or had been committed by his subordinates, and he failed to take the necessary and responsible measures to prevent such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the execution of the crimes of Imprisonment and Cruel Treatment of Serb and Albanian civilians. During the period set forth above, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj unlawfully seized at least 35 Serb and Albanian civilians from the municipalities of Stimlje/Shtime, Glogovac/Gllogoc, Lipljan/Lipjan in Kosovo and forcibly brought them to the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. At the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj unlawfully detained the Serb and Albanian civilians for prolonged periods. Albanian civilian detainees were repeatedly interrogated about alleged "collaboration" with Serbs, often on the basis only of non-military interactions with Serb civilians. Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi personally participated in the guarding of the detainees at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp and in the interrogations of the detainees. By these acts and omissions, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi participated in: Count 1: Imprisonment, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(e), 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 2: Cruel Treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Counts 3 to 5, Torture, Cruel Treatment: From in or about May 1998 through to on or about 25 July 1998, at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp, Fatmir Limaj individually and in concert with KLA forces under his command and control, planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of the crimes of Torture and Cruel Treatment of Serb and Albanian civilians. Fatmir Limaj also knew or had reason to know that the crimes of Torture and Cruel Treatment were about to be committed or had been committed by his subordinates, and he failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the execution of the crimes of Torture and Cruel Treatment of Serb and Albanian civilians. During the time period set forth above, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj held the detainees at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp under conditions that were brutal and inhumane, and routinely subjected them to physical and psychological assault, including torture and beatings. Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi participated in the maintaining and enforcing the inhumane conditions at the camp, which included inadequate food and medical care, and participated in or aided and abetted the torture and beatings of the detainees. By these acts and omissions, Haradin Bala, Isak Musliu, and Agim Murtezi participated in: Count 3: Torture, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(f), 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 4: Torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 5: Cruel Treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 punishable under Articles 3 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Counts 6 to 7, Murder: From a date in or about June 1998 through to 25 July 1998, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj, including Haradin Bala and Isak Musliu planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation, or execution of the crime of Murder of Serb and Albanian civilians at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. In each of the instances set forth below, Fatmir Limaj knew or had reason to know that the crime of Murder was about to be committed or had been committed by his subordinates, and he failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. On a date after 24 June 1998 but before 25 July 1998, KLA forces Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj murdered a number of Serb and non-Albanian detainees at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp whose names are set forth in Annex 1 to this indictment. On a date in or about mid-July 1998, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj beat, tortured, and murdered a number of Serb and Albanian detainees at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp whose names are set forth in Annex II to this indictment. Haradin Bala, and Isak Musliu participated in or aided and abetted the murder of the four detainees. On a date in or about June or July 1998, KLA forces under the command and control of Fatmir Limaj beat, tortured, and murdered Fehmi Xhema, also known as Fehmi Tafa, at the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. Haradin Bala and Isak Musliu participated in or aided and abetted the murder of Fehmi Xhema, also known as Fehmi Tafa. By these acts and omissions, Haradin Bala and Isak Musliu participated in: Count 6: Murder, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 7: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Counts 8 to 9, Murder: On or about 25 July 1998, in or around the Berisa/Berisha mountains near the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp, Fatmir Limaj individually and in concert with KLA forces under his command and control, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation, or execution of the crime of Murder of 11 Albanian detainees. Fatmir Limaj also knew or had reason to know that the crime of Murder was about to be committed or had been committed by his subordinates, and he failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. Haradin Bala and Agim Murtezi committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the execution of, the crime of Murder of the 11 Albanian detainees. Shortly before 25 July 1998, Serb forces retook the area around the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp. As a result, on 25 July 1998, the KLA abandoned the Lapusnik/Llapushnik Prison Camp and Haradin Bala and Agim Murtezi marched approximately 22 detainees from the camp into the Berisa/Berisha mountains. On the way they met up with Fatmir Limaj who gave orders to Haradin Bala and Agim Murtezi. Shortly thereafter, Haradin Bala divided the detainees into two groups. One group of approximately nine detainees was released. The other group of approximately 13 detainees was marched by Haradin Bala, Agim Murtezi, and a third KLA soldier to a clearing in the woods. Haradin Bala, Agim Murtezi, and the third soldier then shot them, killing 11 of the detainees whose names are set forth in Annex III to this indictment. By these acts and omissions, Haradin Bala and Agim Murtezi participated in: Count 8: Murder, a crime against humanity as punishable under Articles 5(a), 7(1), and, Count 9: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Here is a question addressed to Defence counsel. Do your clients know that they must plead to the charges in the indictment within 30 days of the Initial Appearance and if they so wish, they can also do so today? Are they ready to enter a plea today? Yes, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Mr. Bala is aware of that and he is prepared to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, likewise, Mr. Musliu is aware that he has 30 days to enter his plea but he is prepared to enter his plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Murtezi is aware and he is ready to enter a plea today; however, I would like to make submissions before we proceed to the entrance of plea by the -- by Mr. Murtezi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Very quickly, Your Honour, I would like first of all to highlight the fact that even though it is true that I did not have and not a very extensive opportunity to discuss with Mr. Murtezi the content of the indictment, I did say earlier on that he understood the nature of the charges that were contained in the indictment. I would like at this time to highlight the fact that I did receive full cooperation from both the security services of this Tribunal as well as from the language department which have allowed me at the last minute to be able to meet Mr. Murtezi in order to ensure that he did understand the nature of the charges. I would also like to point out for the record, Your Honour, that initially when you asked some questions to Mr. Murtezi, one of those questions was: Mr. Murtezi, do you have a pseudonym? The answer of Mr. Murtezi to this question was, yes, Your Honour, I do have a pseudonym and this pseudonym is Gimi [phoen] and this is not Murrizi, as is stated at paragraph 4 of the indictment I just want to state this for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My next submission, Your Honour, has to do with the order by the President of the Court in which he was -- he has assigned this case to Trial Chamber I. I refer here to the French version of the order by the President on page 2 where there seems to have been probably a typo but I need to bring this to the attention of the Chamber. I will read in French if you allow me, Your Honour. [Interpretation] For these motives deciding that the composition of the Chamber, the first Trial Chamber for the case IT-03-66-I will be as follows: Judge Liu Daquin, Judge Amin El Mahdi, Judge Alphonse Orie. Deciding that the initial appearance of the accused in application of Article Rule 62 of the Rules will take place before Trial Chamber II or a judge -- before a judge thereof. [In English] The fact that it was ordered that the initial appearance of the accused would take place before Trial Chamber II is without a doubt a typo, Your Honour, but I thought I would bring it to the attention of the Chamber. Lastly, I would like to bring your attention to the order by which there was a -- considering the motion of the Prosecutor to lift the order for nondisclosure entered on 27 January which was filed today. You have ordered in the Judge El Mahdi, the confirming judge, has ordered that his order for non-disclosure which was contained in the 27 January confirmation order shall be vacated in full with immediate effect. If I look at the confirmation of the indictment, the order to which Judge El Mahdi was referring to, it says at the end that: "There, in any case," I refer to the disposition paragraph 3 where it says that: "There, in any case be no public disclosure of the supporting material until further order." The effect of the order vacating this order would mean that the supporting material would now be able to be made public. I would request that at this point, Your Honour, that the public -- the supporting material be maintained confidential following this initial appearance until further submission by the parties. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much to bring up those issues. As for the mistake in the President's order, I will talk to him about it. I believe it's a typing mistake. As for the last issue, I'll look into it and see what should be done. Thank you very much. Mr. Bala, would you please stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you now ready to enter pleas to the charges against you in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I propose to read out to you just the charge and then I will ask you how do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty. Your answer in each case should be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's begin. The first count against you is the charge of imprisonment, being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The third is a charge of torture being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fourth count is another charge of torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fifth count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The sixth count is a charge of murder as a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The seventh count is another charge of murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The eighth count is a charge of murder as a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The ninth count is a charge of murder too as a violation of the laws or customs of war, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Musliu, are you now ready to enter pleas to the charges against you in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have listened to the charges carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I feel totally innocent of the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as a rule of this procedure, I'll propose to you that I read out each charge and then ask you how do you plead, guilty or not guilty. Your answer in each case should be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first count against you is the charge of imprisonment being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The third count is a charge of torture being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fourth count is another charge of torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fifth count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The sixth count in the indictment is the eighth count is a charge of murder as a crime against humanity, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The seventh count in the indictment is Count 9 is another charge of murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUSLIU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that Mr. Musliu is charged with counts 6 and 7 of the indictment and not counts 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I might make a mistake. I'll look into it but anyway -- but anyway, those counts are listed in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Yes Your Honour, yes, I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Murtezi, would you please stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to enter pleas to the charges against you in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please. I'll read out to you just the charge and then I will ask you how do you plead to the charge, guilty or not guilty. Your answer in each case may be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first count against you is the charge of imprisonment being a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second count is the charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The third count is a charge of torture being a crime against humanity, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fourth count is another charge of torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The fifth count is the charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The sixth count is a charge of murder as a crime against humanity. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The seventh count is a charge of another murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MURTEZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Entirely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: For the record, if you may allow me to note that the last two --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to -- for the record, I would like to confirm that the last two counts to which the accused entered a plea of not guilty refer to counts 8 and 9 in the indictment and not to counts 6 and 7 which the accused is not charged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have already noted that. Thank you very much. There are also some questions addressed to Defence counsel. I would like to know whether the families of the accused has been informed about their arrest and transfer to The Hague, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not entirely sure of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make sure after this sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, in conference with Mr. Musliu, he confirmed that he had an opportunity to speak to his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not something that I've had the time to discuss with Mr. Murtezi. However, I did discuss with him the circumstances surrounding his arrest by KFOR and he has assured me that all procedures were followed correctly and he is both in a good state of mind and good physical conditions to appear before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another question is that the embassy has been informed about their arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I don't know but I will find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, likewise, I don't know what the relevant embassy would be for Kosovo but those inquiries can be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Likewise, Your Honour, I have not had the opportunity to discuss this topic with Mr. Murtezi but will do at the earliest opportunity. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The registrar will note the pleas of the accused today and it will been entrusted to fix a date for trial when appropriate. An accused is remanded in custody until further order. By the order of the presiding judge of the Trial Chamber I, I is designated as the Pre-Trial Judge. A Status Conference will be scheduled to take place within 120 days of the initial appearance in accordance with the Rule 65 bis and all of you will be informed of that date. At this moment, I would like to remind the Prosecutor of their obligation under Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with regard to the disclosure of the supporting materials within 30 days of today. I would also remind counsel for the accused whether you are continuing to serve as their counsel after today or not, the preliminary motions pursuant to Rule 72 may be filed on behalf of the accused no later than 30 days after disclosure by the Prosecutor pursuant to Rule 62(A)(i). Is there any other matter the Prosecution wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Two matters. First of all, my learned friend, Mr. Bourgon, raised a matter which I was unaware and that is that the order for non-disclosure was lifted in its entirety by Judge El Mahdi. That is not, in fact, what the Prosecutor applied for, so I think it is probably a typographical error but it would be very helpful if, as Mr. Bourgon suggested, that that order for non-disclosure remained in place for supporting material only. It is important that the material remains confidential. And the second matter in respect of the supporting material relevant to the comments that you've just made about the Prosecutor's obligation for disclosure, I have a meeting with Defence counsel at 4.30 at which they will be provided with all of the supporting material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Of course we'll look into the matter concerning that order. Are there any matters that Defence counsel would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No further submissions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. By anyway, I have to tell you the sooner your counsel obtain a permanent Defence counsel, the sooner he will find out what it is all about by the material which the Prosecution will provide to them. So I ask you to make sure before the leave the case that you explain to your client and your current client the importance of moving fast. Well, that's all. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 3.33 p.m.
